quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: ______ guarantees that another driver sees you.

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: Drivers entering a highway from an entrance ramp to your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left portion of your lane so they can share the lane, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles merging onto a highway. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to safely enter the highway.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Use the brakes gradually.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Always be flexible about your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are less than ideal.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so your arms steer, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat with straight arms.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves little space on either side. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Makes a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear.
Protects you in a crash.
Should not be worn while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. In warm weather, leather jackets can help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of the lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and other conditions.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only when the road is wet.
Not often.
Only in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket, leather or sturdy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection. Soft material pants do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Only look five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use turn signals and your brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your motorcycle. Always be ready to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left foot peg
Near the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
See and be seen better.
Go faster.
Set up for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position affects road safety. It helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake to stop and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward to see cross traffic better.
Go through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop where the stop sign tells you to. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will not change.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:

options.text: Never
Only during the day
Only at night
Day and night

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to be more visible to others.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who:

options.text: Have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.
Have a faulty ignition system.
Are distracted by passengers.
Are riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a new motorcycle. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean when you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you as you turn. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you need to stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes hard and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake to the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Shift gears during a turn.
Shift gears before a turn.
Change speed suddenly during a turn.
Brake the entire time through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before a turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn, not during the turn.

questions.question: To maintain control while turning a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look ahead by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, stopping:

options.text: Is easier than riding without a sidecar.
Takes longer than riding without a sidecar.
Is impossible.
Is about the same as riding without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes longer than riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to the motorcycle, which requires more braking force to stop. Downhill riding also increases stopping distance. Both factors together make stopping take longer.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make you unable to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies can make you drowsy and harm your ability to ride safely. Before riding, know how any medication affects your body.
